title: Confidence
description: How strongly the available evidence supports a claim, together with the evidence it is derived from. The evidence array is required and non-empty at every level including UNKNOWN, which is the structural expression of the specification's central invariant: confidence never replaces evidence. A confidence object with no evidence would be an opinion, and the schema makes it impossible to record one.

level.description: The confidence level. Constrained to confidence-levels, whose ordinals are the only comparison Amasario defines. A level is a statement about the evidence, never about the trustworthiness of the thing the evidence concerns.

evidence.description: The evidence this confidence is derived from. Required and non-empty: UNKNOWN confidence still requires the record that establishes the absence, such as an OBSERVATION that a boundary was reached, so that 'we do not know' is itself evidenced and distinguishable from 'nothing was attempted'.

contradictingEvidence.description: Evidence that contradicts the claim. Its presence requires the verification status to be CONFLICTING and the level to be below VERIFIED, a pairing enforced by rule provenance/source-to-build. Recording contradiction in its own field rather than in the rationale is what makes the conflict machine-detectable.

rationale.description: Why this level was assigned, in terms of the evidence. Required in practice for anything other than VERIFIED, so that a level cannot be lowered or raised without a stated reason.

aggregation.description: How this level was computed from other claims, when it was. Absent means the level was assigned directly from the evidence listed here.

strategy.description: The combination rule applied. `minimum_ordinal` is the strategy the specification mandates for combining a path or a conjunction; the others exist so that a producer can record honestly what it actually did.

inputs.description: The claims that were combined, each with the level it contributed. Recorded so that the aggregation is auditable rather than a black-box result.

claim.description: A short statement of the input claim.

level.description: The level this input contributed. References this schema's own level enumeration so the two cannot drift.
